messages.content: You are BioGPT, an expert compiler architect. Translate the provided natural language biological protocol into valid, deterministic BioScript code for execution on a microfluidic biochip.

ASSAY TYPE: Digital Microfluidics for Aerosol Impaction, Extraction, and Colorimetric Detection of Inorganic Ions (Sulfate, Nitrate, Ammonium)

REAGENTS USED:
  - Ambient/Laboratory-Generated Aerosol Sample (impacted directly onto the digital microfluidic chip surface via an integrated 5-nozzle inertial impactor, 1 L/min air flow)
  - Distilled Water (sub-microliter scanning/extraction droplet, ~0.5 uL)
  - Methylthymol Blue (MTB) - Barium Reagent (sulfate colorimetric assay, competitive complexation, detected at 608 nm)
  - Ammonium Colorimetric Reagent (detected at 365 nm)
  - Nitrate Colorimetric Reagent (acidic reagent, detected at 540 nm)
  - Sulfate/Ammonium/Nitrate Liquid Standards (six concentrations each, dispensed from on-chip reservoirs to build calibration curves)

STEPS:
1. Aerosol Collection: Air is drawn through five inertial-impactor nozzles (0.24 mm diameter, 1 L/min total flow) built into the chip's top plate, depositing particles >100 nm in diameter directly onto the CYTOP-coated actuation electrodes of the bottom plate (collection efficiency >95% for particles >100 nm).
2. Extraction: After the air flow is stopped, a sub-microliter distilled-water droplet is dispensed from an on-chip reservoir in oil, actuated through the oil/air interface, and scanned twice across the five-electrode impaction area to fully dissolve the deposited aerosol into a single concentrated extract droplet.
3. Sulfate Calibration: Six standard sulfate concentrations are sequentially dispensed and each mixed with the MTB-Ba reagent; the resulting droplet is actuated between two horizontal optical fibers and absorbance is measured at 608 nm to build a calibration curve (LOD ~11 ppm).
4. Sulfate Sample Measurement: The aerosol extract droplet is mixed with the MTB-Ba reagent and absorbance is measured at 608 nm; the mixed droplet is then discarded.
5. Ammonium Calibration: Six standard ammonium concentrations are sequentially dispensed and each mixed with the ammonium reagent; absorbance is measured at 365 nm to build a calibration curve (LOD ~0.256 ppm).
6. Ammonium Sample Measurement: The aerosol extract droplet is mixed with the ammonium reagent and absorbance is measured at 365 nm; the mixed droplet is then discarded.
7. Nitrate Calibration (unstable): Six standard nitrate concentrations are sequentially dispensed and each mixed with the acidic nitrate reagent; because a precipitate forms over the first 3-4 minutes, droplets are held ~150 s post-mixing before absorbance is measured at 540 nm (nonzero y-intercept observed, indicating reduced sensitivity).
8. Nitrate Sample Measurement: The aerosol extract droplet is mixed with the nitrate reagent, held 150 s, and absorbance is measured at 540 nm; the mixed droplet is then discarded, and the extract droplet itself is discarded once all three assays are complete.

INTERPRETATION: Successful ion quantification is confirmed by linear calibration curves (R^2 ~0.95-0.98) for sulfate and ammonium comparable to off-chip Tecan plate-reader results, on-chip limits of detection of 11 ppm (sulfate) and 0.256 ppm (ammonium) sufficient for converted air-concentration LODs of 0.275 ug/m3 and 6.5 ng/m3 respectively at 1 L/min for 1 h sampling, negligible cross-ion interference, and an unresolved precipitate-driven artifact that prevents stable nitrate quantification on-chip despite a linear off-chip response.

metadata.protocol_name: Digital Microfluidics for the Detection of Selected Inorganic Ions in Aerosols (Huang et al. 2020)

sources.title: Digital Microfluidics for the Detection of Selected Inorganic Ions in Aerosols

metadata.notes: The authored BioScript code is a direct translation of the paper's on-chip aerosol collection/extraction/detection pipeline (Section 2, Figure 2: dispense, transport, collection, mixing, absorbance detection) and the multianalyte calibration procedure of Section 3.2 (six standard concentrations per analyte). Because BioScript's grammar exposes no dedicated inertial-impaction or physical air-sampling primitive, the external aerosol impaction step (5-nozzle impactor, 1 L/min flow, collection efficiency data of Section 3.1/Figure 8) is not itself modeled; only the on-chip extraction droplet that dissolves the deposit (the 'aerosol_sample' manifest, scanned twice per the paper's two-pass dissolution) is captured. The detection modality in the paper is colorimetric spectrophotometry via on-chip optical fibers (fixed wavelengths 365/540/608 nm), not fluorescence, so 'module absorbance' is used in place of the fluorescence module seen in other translated protocols, since BioScript's grammar accepts an arbitrary detect-module identifier rather than hardcoding one. The nitrate branch is modeled with an added 150s heat/hold step (at ambient 25c) reflecting the paper's report that stable absorbance was only reached ~150s after mixing due to precipitate formation from the acidic reagent; the paper explicitly states nitrate measurements were unstable and unreliable on-chip, so the nitrate branch is retained structurally (per the six-concentration calibration pattern used for sulfate/ammonium) but its output is not gated by an LOD-based if/dispose check, unlike the sulfate and ammonium branches, reflecting that no trustworthy on-chip nitrate LOD was established.

the hypothesis is that the acidic reagent in the nitrate assay attacks the coating material

if five relatively more stable measurements at 150 s after mixing are taken, the absorbance and concentration do have the linear relationship

numeric_mismatches.note: The 5-nozzle inertial impactor, its fluid-mechanical design parameters (Reynolds number 3132.7, d50 = 162.7 nm), and the chip-to-world chamber collection-efficiency experiments (Figure 6, Figure 8) describe a physical air-sampling apparatus upstream of the chip; BioScript has no primitive for aerosol impaction itself, so the protocol begins at the on-chip extraction droplet.

numeric_mismatches.field: if-gated dispose logic on sulfate/ammonium readings
numeric_mismatches.note: The thresholds used (>=11 ppm sulfate, >=0.256 ppm ammonium) are the paper's reported LOD values, but the paper does not describe a keep/discard decision branch at these thresholds; the if/dispose structure is invented to fit BioScript's conditional-dispose pattern, not drawn directly from the text.

The paper specifies a ~0.5 uL extraction droplet volume (Vw = 0.5 uL) and a 1:1 mixing ratio with reagents; BioScript's 'units' fields use a normalized value of 1 for all dispense operations rather than the paper's literal microliter volumes, consistent with the relative-volume convention used in the reference translations.

numeric_mismatches.field: circular/back-and-forth droplet actuation during optical-fiber measurement
numeric_mismatches.note: The paper describes the droplet being moved back and forth through the gap between two optical fibers multiple times during measurement (Figure 9); BioScript has no primitive for spatial actuation patterns, so this is folded into the plain 'detect absorbance ... for 5s' step with no positional detail.
